question:
Solve the following system by the inverse-matrix method:
$$2x-y+z=3$$
$$x+y+z=6$$
$$x+2y-z=2$$

(a) Express the system as $AX=B$ and calculate $|A|$.

(b) Obtain $A^{-1}$ and hence find $x$, $y$, and $z$.

(c) Verify the result through matrix multiplication.
explanation:
(a)
The matrix equation is
$$\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 & 1\\1 & 1 & 1\\1 & 2 & -1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\6\\2\end{bmatrix}$$
Thus,
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 & 1\\1 & 1 & 1\\1 & 2 & -1\end{bmatrix}$$
Expanding along the first row,
$$|A|=2(-1-2)+\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1\\1 & -1\end{vmatrix}+\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1\\1 & 2\end{vmatrix}$$
$$|A|=-6-2+1=-7$$

(b)
The adjoint of $A$ is
$$\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 1 & -2\\2 & -3 & -1\\1 & -5 & 3\end{bmatrix}$$
Therefore,
$$A^{-1}=-\frac{1}{7}\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 1 & -2\\2 & -3 & -1\\1 & -5 & 3\end{bmatrix}$$
Now,
$$X=A^{-1}B$$
$$X=-\frac{1}{7}\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 1 & -2\\2 & -3 & -1\\1 & -5 & 3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}3\\6\\2\end{bmatrix}$$
$$X=-\frac{1}{7}\begin{bmatrix}-9+6-4\\6-18-2\\3-30+6\end{bmatrix}=-\frac{1}{7}\begin{bmatrix}-7\\-14\\-21\end{bmatrix}$$
Hence,
$$x=1,\quad y=2,\quad z=3$$

(c)
$$AX=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 & 1\\1 & 1 & 1\\1 & 2 & -1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\\3\end{bmatrix}$$
$$=\begin{bmatrix}3\\6\\2\end{bmatrix}=B$$
Thus, the solution is verified.
